hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeler in Inver Grove Heights for Design and Build
hero.subheadline: McDonald Remodeling has designed and built kitchens, bathrooms and lower levels for Twin Cities homeowners since 2000. Every project is drawn in 3D, priced in a fixed-price contract and scheduled down to the day before work begins.

image.alt: Lakeville kitchen with stained wood and sage green cabinets, a white island with black stools and glass pendants, by McDonald Remodeling, kitchen remodeler in Inver Grove Heights

intro.h2: Challenging designs, finished down to the last detail
paragraphs: McDonald Remodeling is a kitchen remodeler in Inver Grove Heights founded in 2000 and based on Cahill Avenue. As a full-service design/build firm, it handles both the design and the construction, so one company is responsible for the plan and for the finished room.

The team calls challenging design its specialty, and its planning backs that up. Your home is measured and modeled in 3D, layouts are tested before a hammer is lifted, and every task is scheduled down to the day. Clients from Shoreview to Cottage Grove point to that daily schedule as the reason they hired McDonald.

services.h2: Kitchens first, then any room that needs a rethink

items.name: Kitchens
items.blurb: Smart layouts, custom cabinetry and materials picked for beauty and daily use. Recent kitchens include a Bloomington main floor with sage green and wood cabinets, a Lakeville update that blends existing oak with new finishes, and a 100-plus-year-old St. Paul home reworked for modern living.

image.alt: Bloomington kitchen and main floor remodel with sage green and wood cabinets, brass pendants and a gold velvet sofa in the open living area

items.name: Bathrooms
items.blurb: Spa-like primary suites, powder rooms and accessible baths with custom storage and finishes chosen for daily use. McDonald's bath work has earned NARI Contractor of the Year awards in 2022, 2023 and 2024, and one couple hired the team to make a main floor bathroom more accessible as they age.

image.alt: Accessible primary bathroom remodel with a walk-in shower, grab bar, handheld shower, marble-look tile and open towel shelving

items.name: Lower levels
items.blurb: Basements become places to relax or gather, with layout, lighting and materials suited to below-grade space. The Havana After Hours project turned an Inver Grove Heights lower level into a game room, and one couple's 1950s basement was their first remodel ever.

image.alt: Inver Grove Heights lower level remodel with a billiard table, stained wood columns, sage green walls and built-in shelving

items.name: Bars, pool houses and specialty spaces
items.blurb: Some rooms are just for fun: lower-level bars, home libraries, mudrooms with built-in lockers, and even a pool house with an outdoor kitchen. A Mendota Heights family that had worked with McDonald for 17 years added a lower level and bar built around accessibility, openness and natural light.

image.alt: Mendota Heights lower-level bar with dark cabinets, white counters, built-in wine storage and a backlit city skyline photo

items.name: Whole-home and main-level remodels
items.blurb: When several rooms need work, McDonald plans the main level as a whole. One family flipped their kitchen and dining room, converted a fireplace to gas with new stone and remodeled a guest bath in one project, with workers on site nearly every workday.

image.alt: Eden Prairie whole-home remodel kitchen with white cabinets, a stone-topped wood island with built-in bookshelves and pendant lights

why_choose_us.h2: Why Twin Cities homeowners trust McDonald

items.title: Scheduled down to the day
items.text: Tasks are scheduled day by day before construction starts. A Shoreview couple thought it was a sales pitch until every milestone was met, and their neighbors noticed too.

items.title: A fixed price before you build
items.text: The design phase ends with a detailed proposal and a final contract with a fixed price, so the number is settled before the first wall comes down.

items.title: A guest in your home
items.text: Because most families stay home during a remodel, the team treats itself as a guest from the first walk-through to the final clean-up, with a project manager as your contact.

items.title: Awards judged by the industry
items.text: Recent honors include a 2026 Regional Chrysalis Award for a kitchen, 2026 Best of Houzz for Service and Design, and ROMA awards from Housing First Minnesota.

about.h2: Led by owner and CEO Chris Wylie, with roots back to 1976
about.text: Chris Wylie is the owner and CEO of McDonald Remodeling, the design/build firm founded in 2000 and based on Cahill Avenue in Inver Grove Heights. Its values of quality design and craftsmanship trace back to 1976, when Jim McDonald built his first home. Today the firm has a dedicated interior design studio with designers such as Alisa Dragt-Hoffman and Emily Thull, plus project managers and construction superintendents. Its mission is remodeling and design rooted in honesty, integrity, creativity and meticulous attention to detail, and its employees give hundreds of volunteer hours each year.

process.h2: Four phases, each with a timeframe you can plan around

steps.title: Discovery (about 1 to 2 weeks)
steps.text: A home visit to talk through your ideas, their benefits and challenges, ending with a well-reasoned view of what is possible and an approximate budget.

steps.title: Design (about 1 to 2 months)
steps.text: Under a design agreement, the team measures your home, tests layouts in 3D software and delivers a detailed proposal with a fixed-price contract.

steps.title: Refinement (about 1 to 2 months)
steps.text: Design and selection meetings with the interior designers settle wood finishes, cabinetry, fixtures, paint, tile and flooring until every element is chosen.

steps.title: Construction (depends on scope)
steps.text: Tasks are scheduled down to the day, your project manager keeps you informed, and the job closes with a thorough walkthrough of the finished space.

service_area.h2: Kitchen remodeler in Inver Grove Heights serving the Twin Cities
service_area.text: McDonald Remodeling works from 6015 Cahill Ave E, Suite 100, in Inver Grove Heights and serves St. Paul, Minneapolis, the surrounding metro and Western Wisconsin. Communities it has worked in include Eagan, Woodbury, Mendota Heights, Apple Valley, Lakeville, Bloomington, Edina, Eden Prairie, Roseville, Shoreview, Stillwater, Lake Elmo, Minnetonka and Hudson. Not on the list? Call (651) 554-1234 and the office will tell you whether your address is in range.

items.q: How long does a remodel take?
items.a: McDonald's process page gives rough timeframes for each phase: discovery takes about 1 to 2 weeks, design about 1 to 2 months, and refinement of selections about 1 to 2 months. Construction time depends on the scope and size of your project, and every task is scheduled down to the day before work begins.

items.q: Do I need to move out during construction?
items.a: Most families don't. McDonald notes that remodeling is almost always done while homeowners keep living in the home, so the crew acts as a guest from the first walk-through to the final clean-up. One Edina couple was out of state for their whole project and got regular updates by email, photos and videos.

items.q: Does McDonald help with design and selections?
items.a: Yes. The firm has a dedicated interior design studio. During refinement you meet with its interior designers to choose wood finishes, cabinetry, fixtures, paint, tile and flooring. One client said designer Alisa had everything displayed when they arrived and could put a tile's texture and color up on screen to help them decide.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom or home more accessible?
items.a: Yes. One Google reviewer hired McDonald to remodel a main floor bathroom so it would be more accessible as the couple ages, and a Mendota Heights lower level was designed around accessibility, openness and natural light. Another family, whose toddler uses a wheelchair, wrote that the design removed obstacles and made them feel safe at home.

items.q: Is McDonald licensed, and what awards has it won?
items.a: McDonald holds Minnesota license #BC205832. Recent recognition includes a 2026 Regional Chrysalis Award for a kitchen, 2026 Best of Houzz for Service and Design, a 2026 Best of the Twin Cities Readers' Poll silver from Mpls. St. Paul Magazine, 2025 and 2024 ROMA awards from Housing First Minnesota, and NARI Contractor of the Year bath awards.

final_cta.h2: Start the conversation about your kitchen
final_cta.text: Call McDonald Remodeling in Inver Grove Heights or send a note through the Connect form.
